checkpointRows.reviewQuestion: Which PWG source record(s) should define the target gam primary series, and which should remain retained side evidence?
checkpointRows.note: Source lines verified in local csl-orig. L21814 (pc 2-0666) is the vol-2 primary article of 1. gam = target-primary-series; L72578 (5-1369) and L119742 (7-1737) are vol-5/7 Nachtraege ('streiche', 'lies' correction language) = same-headword-supplement, with L119742 carrying div n="p" preverb material = prefixed-or-derived-series; L21815 (2-0685, h=2) is 2. gam 'Erde' = separate-homonym. div n="1"/"2" runs = candidate-sense-marker; supplement records flagged via supplement-marker.

checkpointRows.reviewQuestion: Which PWG source record(s) should define the target dharma primary series, and which should remain retained side evidence?
checkpointRows.note: Source lines verified. L36241 (pc 3-0882) is the vol-3 primary Da/rma article = target-primary-series; L76490 (5-1520) is a vol-5 Nachtrag ('fuege noch ... hinzu', 'liest die ed. Bomb.') = same-headword-supplement. div n="1"/"2" markers = candidate-sense-marker.

checkpointRows.reviewQuestion: Do the proposed marker-run or source-record labels identify the parser window for gam in BEN while retaining non-target rows?
checkpointRows.note: Single source record L4326 (172 rows). Benfey's numbered {@1.@} runs restart at each preverb section, so the 172 rows are an expansion of reset runs; the archived 23 senses correspond to the main (pre-preverb) numbered run. archive-prefix-runs defines the target window; reset-run-expansion explains the drift. Later preverb runs stay retained, not counted.

checkpointRows.reviewQuestion: Do the proposed marker-run or source-record labels identify the parser window for rama in BEN while retaining non-target rows?
checkpointRows.note: L11986 (rama, 'Pleasing; husband; Lakshmi') and L12079 (rAma, 'Beautiful; hero of the Ramayana') are distinct lemmas bundled by lookup normalization. Exact-headword record L11986 = target for lemma rama; rAma record split out of the bundle as its own lemma, retained as evidence only.

checkpointRows.reviewQuestion: Which AE reverse rank bands for gam should be reviewed as direct equivalents, and which should remain context or overmatch evidence?
checkpointRows.note: Band vocabulary accepted, but every sampled reverse row for gam is a phrase/collocation match ('go abroad' -> prakASatAM gam under Abroad; similarly accede, accrue, advance, agree). For verbal lemmas AE reverse rows are context evidence, not sense alignments; the 243-row set stays side evidence under the band labels. See dharma:ae for the nominal counterpart where banding is promoted.

checkpointRows.reviewQuestion: Which AE reverse rank bands for dharma should be reviewed as direct equivalents, and which should remain context or overmatch evidence?
checkpointRows.note: dharma is nominal: AE contains genuine direct equivalents alongside collocational uses (Administer -> Darma-nyAya-vivecanaM kf is collocational; Law/Duty/Religion-type headwords carry direct equivalents). Promote the rank-band scheme for nominal lemmas: high band -> direct-equivalent review, tail bands remain context/overmatch evidence. Verb lemmas stay side evidence per gam:ae.

checkpointRows.reviewQuestion: Which VCP iti units for dharma are definition, authority, grammar, or discussion evidence rather than reviewed senses?
checkpointRows.note: Record L27030 verified: opens with derivation (Df--man, ardDarccA0), then the Mimamsa definition 'codanAlakzaRo'rTo DarmaH' with Jaimini siglum (jE0 sUtra), followed by extended Sabara-bhasya discussion (aTAto DarmajijYAsA passage). The three unit labels map exactly: definition units, authority-siglum units, and long commentarial discussion that must not be counted as senses. Archive 9 vs source 27 is commentary inflation, as expected.

checkpointRows.reviewQuestion: Which SKD iti units for dharma are definition, authority, grammar, or discussion evidence rather than reviewed senses?
checkpointRows.note: Records L17667 (puM klI) and L17668 (puM) verified: SKD genuinely splits DarmmaH into two consecutive gender-based records = same-headword-record-split. L17667 carries definition (SuBAdfzwam), the Amara paryaya run (puRyam, SreyaH, sukftam, vfzaH ityamaraH), and Medini/Hemacandra authority units with yaTA quotations (Hitopadesa, Mahabharata, Yogasara) = definition-iti-unit + authority-quotation-unit.

checkpointRows.packetTitle: Source gaps, mild drift, and parity controls
checkpointRows.reviewQuestion: Should iti in AP remain a parser control or follow-up row, and do the source pointers explain the archive comparison drift?
checkpointRows.note: Record L8130 verified: the long first sense block under one marker contains nested (1), (2)... subdivisions the splitter does not open = nested-marker-gap, explaining the 3-vs-5 under-split; the :preface lumped-proxy row = preface-proxy-extra. Real marker-coverage gap; keep visible as side evidence for a later nested-marker pass, not in the target window.

checkpointRows.packetTitle: Source gaps, mild drift, and parity controls
checkpointRows.reviewQuestion: Should gam in AP remain a parser control or follow-up row, and do the source pointers explain the archive comparison drift?
checkpointRows.note: Exact archive parity (16=16) verified: L13831 is the main gam article; L13731.006 is an empty {{Lbody=13731.004}} continuation pointer = continuation-proxy-row. Use as positive parser-parity regression control. nested-marker-gap dropped from the accepted set: parity at ratio 1.0 demonstrates no gap on this row.

archiveParityPolicy: Archive parity is a comparison/control signal for drift review and regression checks, not the optimization target.
limitations: This artifact mirrors the recorded human checkpoint decisions; it does not itself promote parser behavior.
Proposed parser labels explain drift classes and review scope; the accepted subset for each checkpoint row lives in reviewedValue.acceptedParserLabels.
10 of 10 checkpoint rows carry complete human decisions; 0 remain needs-review with empty human fields.
Parser promotion is gated by each checkpoint row's recorded parserDisposition and stays scoped to the documented promotion experiment.
No R2 splitter behavior, source-anchor generation, H5 review rows, public R2 pages, backend, runtime LLM, corpus, DCS, or standards work is changed.
boundaryNote: Dictionary source rows, existing R2 source anchors, recovered archive fixtures, machine label proposals, and the human-decided R2 checkpoint review overlay only.
